title: Resting pulse (60-second) reference distributions, US males 18+, NHANES 2015-2018
private_note: Population reference only; contains no personal data.

source.survey: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), CDC National Center for Health Statistics
source.suggested_citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS). National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey Data, 2015-2016 and 2017-2018. Hyattsville, MD: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, CDC.

variables.BPXPLS: 60 sec. pulse (30 sec. pulse * 2), bpm; taken by MEC examiner, seated after 5 min rest. Values are even numbers.
variables.BPXPULS: Pulse regular/irregular (not used as a filter)
variables.RIDAGEYR: Age in years at screening (top-coded at 80)

method.population: Males (RIAGENDR=1), age 18+ at screening, with non-missing BPXPLS; 75+ band includes top-coded age 80.
method.weighting: 4-year combined weight = WTMEC2YR / 2 (NCHS guidance for combining 2 cycles).
method.mean_sd: Survey-weighted mean; weighted population SD (sqrt of weighted variance).
method.se_mean: Taylor-series linearization for a domain ratio mean, strata x PSU, with-replacement; full exam sample kept in design; df = #PSU - #strata.
method.quantiles: BPXPLS is recorded in 2-bpm steps (30-s count x 2). Each reported value v is treated as spread uniformly over [v-1, v+1); weighted CDF is piecewise-linear; percentiles invert that CDF (so they can be non-integer). percentile_lookup gives this CDF x 100 at each integer bpm 40-110.
method.density: Survey-weighted Gaussian KDE on 40-110 bpm, 1-bpm grid. Bandwidth = Silverman's rule of thumb 0.9 * min(weighted SD, weighted IQR/1.34) * n_eff^(-1/5), n_eff = (sum w)^2 / sum(w^2) (Kish). Density units: per bpm.

global_facts: Across age bands, the median measured resting pulse ranges from about 66 bpm (75+) to about 72 bpm (18–24).

facts: Half of US men 18–24 have a measured resting pulse between 64 and 80 bpm (middle 50%).
The median measured resting pulse for men 18–24 is about 72 bpm; the weighted mean is 73.0 bpm (SD 11.8).
90% of men 18–24 fall between about 56 and 93 bpm.
A pulse of 60 bpm sits at about the 15th percentile for men 18–24; 70 bpm at about the 42nd.
About 13% of men 18–24 had a recorded pulse below 60 bpm, and about 2% above 100 bpm.
The median for men 18–24 is 2 bpm higher than the median for all men 18+ (70 bpm).
